targets.review_note: Group row strings by their count vector; group weight is its multinomial multiplicity. Beautiful formations are ordered selections of N distinct groups weighted by these multiplicities, N! times an elementary symmetric polynomial. Compute power sums by coefficient extraction of (sum x^c/(c!)^j)^K times(M!)^j, then Newton identities. This preserves row order and within-row permutations.

targets.review_note: Polycarp wins if his Manhattan arrival time is no later than Vasiliy Chebyshev arrival time, including first-move tie. He also wins when coordinatewise southwest, using blocking to prevent the diagonal player passing him. Otherwise Vasiliy has both a strict timing advantage and a free axis to bypass. Both nonnegative boundaries and skip moves are included in independent finite-state game checks.

targets.review_note: Burnside average grouped by permutation cycle partitions. One length-l cycle yields floor(l/2) internal edge orbits; two cycles yield gcd(lengths) cross-edge orbits. A partition contributes m^orbits divided by product(length^count*count!). Recursion updates both orbit count and reciprocal multiplicity, valid since prime modulus exceeds n. Colors remain labeled; vertices are quotiented.

No unstated bounded-primality shortcut.
